name: Glossary & Acronym Book
blurb: a project's acronyms and terms in one list
intro: The project's acronyms and terms in one list, saved as the project's record in the app: one term, one meaning (ISO 704), with duplicates and conflicting expansions flagged. Paste a note or a spec to find the acronyms it uses that the glossary does not define yet.

inputs.label: Terms
inputs.help: The same term may mean different things in two rooms: give each its Domain.

default.definition: A short record of why a part or topology was chosen.
Every part on the board with quantity, value and order number.
Checks the layout against the fab's clearances and widths.
Checks the schematic for unconnected pins and driver conflicts.
A static spark; USB ports are tested to IEC 61000-4-2.
A diode that clamps ESD and surge on a line.
A linear regulator that works with little headroom.
Two-wire bus (SDA, SCL) with open-drain lines and pull-ups.
The self-lit display; here an SSD1306 128x32.
3D printing by extruding a plastic filament.

inputs.label: Search
inputs.placeholder: term or a word of its meaning

inputs.label: Check a text for undefined acronyms
inputs.default: The PCB passed DRC and ERC. Next: add a TVS on the USB lines for ESD, route SWD to the header, and check the UART level shifter. OTA is still off.
inputs.placeholder: Paste a note, a spec or a README

usage: Pass `terms` as rows {term, expansion, definition, domain: all|project|cad|pcb|web|embedded|mobile, see}, optionally `domain`/`filter` to narrow the list and `text` to scan a document. It returns the sorted glossary, warnings for duplicates, conflicting meanings in one domain and dangling see-also links, and - for a text - the acronyms used but not defined (with where they first appear), plus Markdown and CSV. Read the project's glossary with the MCP tool tool_data (id glossary) before writing documentation, and add new terms to it (data {terms: [...]}).
sources: ISO 704:2022 Terminology work - Principles and methods (one concept, one term)
IEC 60050 International Electrotechnical Vocabulary (electropedia.org) for standard electrical definitions
